# Experience and delivery

Use the applicable parts. A static asset does not need a state machine; an
unfamiliar format does need its own requirements before web defaults are applied.

## Scope the experience

Extend the task model with what changes the design: the outcome; medium and
supported inputs; arrival, interruption and return; people affected and permissions;
access, language and environment; final host and export format. Establish objects,
labels, navigation and information needed together before arranging screens.

Apply Decision 0's evidence and uncertainty rules to the experience model. Model
role-play and screenshot critique are not observed user research.

For unfamiliar media or platforms, consult current authoritative guidance for the
actual target and identify unavailable specialist verification. Do not infer that
browser checks establish native-file, media, device or assistive-technology behavior.

## Continuity and consequences

For stateful work, distinguish saved, unsaved, pending, failed and stale state where
they can occur. Name what persists and when an action commits. Exercise interruption,
return, retry and recovery; shared work also needs applicable permission and conflict
paths. Offline writes are a product choice, not a universal requirement.

Make consequential effects, recipients and disclosure clear before commitment.
Keep decline, correction, cancellation and exit understandable where applicable.
A higher completion or engagement rate cannot offset unintended actions, lost work
or misleading commitments. Protect rare consequential paths alongside frequent work.

For AI behavior, communicate capabilities and limits, distinguish suggestion from
committed action, and support correction, stopping and recovery. Test a plausible
wrong answer and misunderstood request, including what changes over time.

## Medium-specific probes

| Medium or condition | What to inspect and exercise |
|---|---|
| Multi-page services, search and account flows | Deep-link arrival, finding the right object, backtracking, handoffs, recovery and exit; preserve orientation and relevant progress. |
| Native apps, wearables, TV and kiosks | Actual platform semantics, supported input and window/device configurations; text enlargement, interruption and return. Target-specific ergonomics require the target device. |
| PDF, document, EPUB or reading deck | The final file in its intended host: reading order, headings, tables, links, navigation, enlargement and required print/export properties. |
| Spreadsheet or structured workbook | Named sheets/tables, headers, editable inputs versus formulas, units and errors; change an input and read its result with keyboard and relevant assistive navigation. |
| Charts, maps and scientific figures | Source, units, scale, uncertainty and missing data; decode the important comparison and check equivalent access. Use domain methods for geographic or scientific claims. |
| Email, notifications and messages | Supported clients, narrow/dark rendering, blocked images, destination, dismissal and relevant preference controls; inspect the received artifact. |
| Audio, video, animation or synchronized media | Timing, playback and appropriate captions, descriptions and transcripts. They serve different needs; inspect essential content through each required alternative. |
| Voice and conversation | Silence, misrecognition, interruption, changed parameter, cancellation and consequential confirmation; retain context through repair. |
| CLI and developer tools | Help, error recovery, exit status, human versus machine output, pipes, noninteractive use and cancellation. Full-screen terminal UIs also need navigation/focus checks. |
| Games, simulations and creative tools | The core interaction, useful feedback, mistakes, recovery, pause and return where supported. Interaction may carry the purpose; test equivalent access to essential meaning and controls. |
| Spatial or embodied experiences | Orientation, input remapping, comfort, pause and safe exit on the actual hardware; relevant alternate inputs and outputs. |
| Brand, image and print/export assets | Intended small and large uses, supported backgrounds, recognition, required formats and production specifications. Verify supplied evidence; do not fabricate it. |

## Access and delivery evidence

Apply the relevant standard and platform guidance with its level, units and
exceptions. Preserve semantics and equivalent access through export. Test the
supported languages, mixed direction, long strings and locale formatting in their
actual containers. For shared or consequential work, include affected people and
permission changes in the probe.

Choose evidence by property: screenshots for composition; playback for timing;
interaction for task completion; native structure and assistive use for semantics.
Record the host, format, device/input and states covered. Identify required checks
that could not run; a proxy preview cannot silently substitute for them.
